final_message:
I've written `answer.json`. Four functions in `billing/subscriptions.py` emit `subscription.updated` directly:

- `subscriptions.transition` emits it for every status change except to `canceled`, which emits `subscription.canceled` instead.
- `subscriptions.change_items` emits it after replacing the items.
- `subscriptions.cancel` emits it when cancelling at period end. A cancel that takes effect immediately goes through `transition` and emits `subscription.canceled`.
- `subscriptions.reactivate` emits it when it clears the scheduled cancellation.

I read the emit calls in `subscriptions.py`, `dunning.py` and `refunds.py`, and grepped the rest of the package for the event string. I didn't run the tests, since no code changed. I didn't read through the other modules' emit calls individually, so a call elsewhere that builds the event type some other way would have been missed.

`pause` and `resume` call `transition`, so they're callers and aren't listed.

steps.command: cd billing; sed -n 30,70p subscriptions.py; sed -n 120,200p subscriptions.py; grep -rn "emit\|EventType\|event=" *.py | grep -v "^subscriptions.py" | head -60
cd billing; grep -n "emit(" -A3 subscriptions.py dunning.py refunds.py | grep -v "^--" | head -80; grep -rn "Event(\|\"type\"" *.py | head
